inputs.text: This is not just about recovering money from Mary Ngechi Ngethe. The court found she played a central role in buying unsuitable cemetery land for Ksh.283 million—a stark example of how weak public oversight can turn essential community needs into opportunities for abuse. The people who rely on public services are left carrying the cost. Accountability must reach beyond one official and include reforms that prevent procurement decisions from putting public money ahead of public need.
